subject: EdgeHealth operational runbook & temporary egress clarifications
messages:
From: Lina Park <lina.park@edgehealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeHealth Legal <legal@edgehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify region pinning / emergency cross-region pathing

Hi Sergio,

Quick follow-up from our security team after the demo: we need clearer commitments on two items before procurement can sign the SOW.

1) Region pinning guarantee — can you confirm that customer production data (requests and model outputs) will be pinned to the US region for EdgeHealth, and under what explicit conditions Redwood would process data outside the US?

2) Temporary cross-region processing — we understand transient failover is supported. Please confirm maximum window length (hours), whether any customer PII or logs are exported outside the pinned region during that window, and what telemetry/audit evidence you can provide after an event.

3) KMS / key custody — who controls the KMS keys in failover scenarios? Are keys replicated cross-region or kept in-region?

We attached the DPA questions list for reference. Can someone on your side provide a short operational runbook and the notification cadence you commit to for any cross-region event?

Thank you,
Lina Park
Head of Cloud Security, EdgeHealth
[Attachment: EdgeHealth-DPA-questions.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify region pinning / emergency cross-region pathing

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Monica (Customer Success) and Karthik (Infra) and Marissa (Legal) so we can give operational, technical, and contract-level answers.

High-level answers up front:
- Redwood supports region pinning for production workloads. Your primary tenancy and model-serving paths will be anchored to the US region.
- We allow transient cross-region processing for emergency failover and capacity bursts; we won’t use cross-region processing for routine load balancing.

Karthik, can you confirm the maximum transient window we currently propose and any constraints on PII/log egress? Monica, I attached a short runbook draft (see attachment) — please review. Marissa, can you outline the DPA addendum route if EdgeHealth wants to lock down the transient window in the contract?

Next steps: Karthik will provide a technical narrative + telemetry list; Marissa will propose contract language and DocuSign path; Monica and I will propose two canary dates for an operational test.

Thanks — Sergio
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Lina Park <lina.park@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jun 2025 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify region pinning / emergency cross-region pathing

Thanks — technical details below (keeping it practical):

1) Region pinning behavior
- Primary: All production requests, model inputs, and generated outputs are served in the US region you select and are routed to US-hosted GPU pools. Customers can pin to a single region via the tenant configuration in the Console.
- Exceptions: Transient cross-region processing is permitted only under two conditions: (a) emergency failover when US capacity is impaired or (b) customer-approved burst overflow (explicit opt-in).

2) Maximum window and retention
- Default maximum transient window: 48 hours for automated emergency failover. We can negotiate a longer, documented window (e.g., 72 hours) in an addendum, but it requires explicit DPA language.
- Data handling during window: We do not persist PII outside the pinned region. Operational caches (KV cache / prefix cache) may be populated in the failover region but are configured with TTL <= 24 hours by default and are purged after failover ends. Audit logs that record control-plane events may be replicated to our central ops region for post-mortem; content-sensitive logs (payload-level request/response) are not replicated unless you opt into telemetry export.

3) KMS and keys
- Keys: Customer-controlled CMKs via Redwood KMS integration (customer-managed keys) remain in the pinned region by default. In emergency failover we can perform key-bridging (ephemeral wrapping keys) to decrypt cached KV segments in the backup region — this is an opt-in behavior that we will not enable without written authorization.

4) Telemetry & evidence we provide after an event
- Event timeline (ISO timestamps) with routing map (which region served each request)
- Token-level latency/cost summary for the window
- Audit log extract (control-plane events) and optional request-sample hashes to validate content governance (no plaintext payloads unless explicitly requested)
- Proof of cache purge and TTL expirations (runbook step logs)

5) Operational controls you can configure today
- Auto-failover: on/off
- Max failover duration: default 48h, can open a support ticket to extend live incidents
- Notifications: immediate pager plus follow-up email and postmortem within 72h

Attachment: I attached the runbook draft with example CLI commands and playbook steps.

If EdgeHealth wants the 48h default reduced (e.g., 24h) or locked at 72h maximum in contract, we can add that to a DPA addendum.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood
[Attachment: redwood-transient-egress-runbook-draft.md (text/markdown)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@edgehealth.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 11:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify region pinning / emergency cross-region pathing

Lina / Sergio — quick legal note on the contractual path:

1) DPA addendum: we have a short DPA addendum template that records (a) the pinned region, (b) the maximum transient window, (c) subprocessor notification timing, and (d) KMS key handling during failover. If EdgeHealth wants a non-negotiable 72-hour ceiling or a shorter 24-hour ceiling, we can attach that to the Master DPA.

2) Subprocessors: Redwood publishes a public subprocessor roster and will provide an up-to-date roster as an annex. Our standard notice period for subprocessor activation is 30 days; we can provide expedited notification and evidence for subprocessors used specifically for failover capacity (logs, certs) as part of the addendum.

3) Evidence and attestation: we can include a clause requiring a post-event attestation within 10 business days with the telemetry items Karthik listed; for particularly sensitive customers we can agree to quarterly attestation reports.

4) Signature path: I'll prepare the DPA addendum and send via DocuSign. Link will include the specific runbook snapshot as an annex so the runbook steps are part of the contract exhibit.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Lina Park <lina.park@edgehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, EdgeHealth Legal <legal@edgehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 14:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify region pinning / emergency cross-region pathing

Thanks — this is very helpful and addresses most of our questions. A few quick asks before we proceed to the addendum:

- Can you confirm the default TTL for any ephemeral KV caches is <= 24 hours (we want that in writing)?
- For the canary, we prefer a weekday morning window; Monica, Sergio — can you propose two slots next week?
- Please include the public subprocessor roster as an annex and highlight any subprocessors that would be used during failover.

If you include the TTL and the subprocessors in the addendum, EdgeHealth Legal is fine to move to DocuSign. Happy to schedule the canary once we have the DPA snapshot.

Regards,
Lina
Head of Cloud Security, EdgeHealth
